dataset_id.description:
A unique ID for this dataset, without the project name. The ID
must contain only letters (a-z, A-Z), numbers (0-9), or
underscores (_). The maximum length is 1,024 characters.
dataset_id.rationale: Identifier of the dataset the access entry targets. It is a resource reference, not a control; access is governed by the principal/role fields, so there is nothing generic to enforce on the name.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

domain.description:
A domain to grant access to. Any users signed in with the
domain specified will be granted the specified access
domain.rationale: Grants dataset access to every user signed in with a named domain. It is not a public principal (allUsers/allAuthenticatedUsers), and restricting it would mean hardcoding the org's allowed domain(s), which a generic platform policy cannot know – overreaching.

group_by_email.description: An email address of a Google Group to grant access to.
group_by_email.rationale: Grants dataset access to a specific Google Group by email. It is a specific (non-public) principal; we cannot generically constrain which group without hardcoding an email, and a group email is not a public/wildcard grant, so there is nothing useful to enforce.

iam_member.description:
Some other type of member that appears in the IAM Policy but isn't a user,
group, domain, or special group. For example: 'allUsers'
iam_member.rationale: A raw IAM member string for dataset access that can include public principals such as allUsers. A policy should reject public (allUsers/allAuthenticatedUsers) and wildcard principals here to prevent broad data exposure, while allowing specific users/groups.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

role.description:
Describes the rights granted to the user specified by the other
member of the access object. Basic, predefined, and custom roles are
supported. Predefined roles that have equivalent basic roles are
swapped by the API to their basic counterparts, and will show a diff
post-create. See
[official docs](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/access-control).
role.rationale: Specifies the IAM role granted in the dataset access entry. A platform policy should not dictate which roles teams may assign; we instead constrain the principals (public/wildcard) rather than the role catalog.

special_group.description:
A special group to grant access to. Possible values include:
* 'projectOwners': Owners of the enclosing project.
* 'projectReaders': Readers of the enclosing project.
* 'projectWriters': Writers of the enclosing project.
* 'allAuthenticatedUsers': All authenticated BigQuery users.
special_group.rationale: Grants dataset access to a special group such as projectOwners/projectReaders or, critically, allAuthenticatedUsers. A policy should reject the public option (allAuthenticatedUsers) to prevent broad data exposure while allowing the project-scoped groups.

user_by_email.description:
An email address of a user to grant access to. For example:
fred@example.com
user_by_email.rationale: Grants dataset access to a specific user by email. It is a specific (non-public) principal; constraining which user is granted access would require hardcoding an email, and a single user is not a public/wildcard grant, so a generic policy adds no security value.

condition.description:
Condition for the binding. If CEL expression in this field is true, this
access binding will be considered.

condition.description.description:
Description of the expression. This is a longer text which describes the expression,
e.g. when hovered over it in a UI.

condition.expression.description: Textual representation of an expression in Common Expression Language syntax.

condition.location.description:
String indicating the location of the expression for error reporting, e.g. a file
name and a position in the file.
condition.location.rationale: Specifies the geographic location associated with the dataset access condition. Treated as a residency control, a policy can require it fall within an approved region whitelist to meet sovereignty requirements.

condition.title.description:
Title for the expression, i.e. a short string describing its purpose.
This can be used e.g. in UIs which allow to enter the expression.

dataset.description: Grants all resources of particular types in a particular dataset read access to the current dataset.

dataset.target_types.description:
Which resources in the dataset this entry applies to. Currently, only views are supported,
but additional target types may be added in the future. Possible values: VIEWS

dataset.dataset.description: The dataset this entry applies to

dataset.dataset.dataset_id.description: The ID of the dataset containing this table.

dataset.dataset.project_id.description: The ID of the project containing this table.

routine.description:
A routine from a different dataset to grant access to. Queries
executed against that routine will have read access to tables in
this dataset. The role field is not required when this field is
set. If that routine is updated by any user, access to the routine
needs to be granted again via an update operation.

routine.dataset_id.description: The ID of the dataset containing this table.

routine.project_id.description: The ID of the project containing this table.

routine.routine_id.description:
The ID of the routine. The ID must contain only letters (a-z,
A-Z), numbers (0-9), or underscores (_). The maximum length
is 256 characters.

view.description:
A view from a different dataset to grant access to. Queries
executed against that view will have read access to tables in
this dataset. The role field is not required when this field is
set. If that view is updated by any user, access to the view
needs to be granted again via an update operation.

view.dataset_id.description: The ID of the dataset containing this table.

view.project_id.description: The ID of the project containing this table.

view.table_id.description:
The ID of the table. The ID must contain only letters (a-z,
A-Z), numbers (0-9), or underscores (_). The maximum length
is 1,024 characters.
